name: Open solder jumper
description: Close the gap between two lands with solder.

citation.document: Footprint For Solderable Jumper?, firsthand rectangular-pad example (https://www.pcblibraries.com/forum/footprint-for-solderable-jumper_topic2089.html). SparkFun, How to Work with Jumper Pads and PCB Traces (https://learn.sparkfun.com/tutorials/how-to-work-with-jumper-pads-and-pcb-traces); JLCPCB, Stencil Capabilities (https://jlcpcb.com/capabilities/pcb-stencil-manufacturing).

note: Each land is 0.5 × 1 mm with 0.2 mm between lands. The illustrative bead spans the land width. Its 0.15 mm height uses a standard JLCPCB stencil thickness as a modelling reference. Actual solder height depends on assembly.

name: Cuttable jumper
description: Open a normally closed trace by cutting it.

citation.document: Footprint For Solderable Jumper?, firsthand rectangular-pad example (https://www.pcblibraries.com/forum/footprint-for-solderable-jumper_topic2089.html). SparkFun, How to Work with Jumper Pads and PCB Traces (https://learn.sparkfun.com/tutorials/how-to-work-with-jumper-pads-and-pcb-traces); SparkFun, PCB Design Specifications (https://learn.sparkfun.com/tutorials/retired---how-to-sell-your-widget-on-sparkfun/all).

note: The 0.5 × 1 mm lands have a 0.2 mm gap. The original cuttable layout uses the 6 mil trace width in SparkFun’s published manufacturing specifications.
